_readme: Migrations whose effects `npm run check:migrations` CANNOT SEE, and where each one stands on prod.
The schema drift check compares live tables and columns. A migration that changes neither — a cron
schedule, a data-only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, a dropped column, a created or replaced function — is
invisible to it: it reports 'prod in sync' whether or not that migration was ever applied. The miss
is silent in both directions (nothing 500s, no gate turns red, the product renders perfectly), which
is how migration 264 sat outstanding on prod while the check reported green.
`scripts/check-manual-prod-migrations.mjs` derives the CANDIDATE LIST from the migration files
themselves, so a new schema-invisible migration cannot avoid needing an entry here. Declaring one is
a decision point, not paperwork: the session that writes the migration is the session that knows
prod:  applied     confirmed on prod — put the anchor (date / Amplify job) in the note
pending     must be applied at or before the next promote — BLOCKS a promote
held        deliberately not applied, an owner decision — does not block, stays visible
unverified  nobody has checked — BLOCKS a promote; resolving it is a one-minute lookup
grandfatheredThrough: migrations at or below this number predate the gate and are not audited.
Raising it is a deliberate act; lowering it means auditing more history.

286_one_word_one_line_on_a_plan.sql.note: Applied to prod 2026-09-10 and verified by querying production directly: 0 twin groups left, the partial unique index present, lines 21 -> 20, 0 orphaned periods, 0 dues schedules unlinked. ⚠ IT MUST GO ON BEFORE THE PROMOTE, AND THE MASTER BUILD IS WHAT ENFORCES THAT — check-schema-parity runs only on master and FAILED job 263 on this exact index, so a plan to apply it after a green build cannot work: the build is not green until it is applied. The cost of that ordering is a short window where prod runs the OLD code (which inserts budget lines with no duplicate handling) against the new rule; bounded by the rebuild, and unavoidable. Original note: Part 1 JOINS duplicate budget lines on one word (data-only, invisible to every drift check); part 2 adds the partial unique index that keeps them joined (visible). Applied to dev 2026-09-09 and verified there by query: 0 twin groups left, every split still sums to its total, no orphaned periods. PROD STILL HOLDS ONE TWIN PAIR (measured 2026-09-09: 1 group, 2 lines, neither carrying a note, on 1 of 4 plans) — the join must run on prod BEFORE the index, which this file does in order. Apply before promoting the code that reads one line per word.

287_a_player_hands_in_more_than_once.sql.note: Applied to prod 2026-09-10 and verified by querying production directly: the UNIQUE (fundraiser_id, player_id) rule is gone and all 8 entries are intact. Safe ahead of its code because the deployed route has no ON CONFLICT naming those columns (checked against origin/master before applying) — dropping the rule cannot break a writer that never relied on it. Original note: Drops UNIQUE (fundraiser_id, player_id) so a player can hand money in to a drive more than once. Applied to dev 2026-09-10; PROD STILL HOLDS THE CONSTRAINT. ⚠ THIS IS THE FIRST 'drop-constraint' ENTRY AND THE GATE COULD NOT SEE IT UNTIL THIS MIGRATION ADDED THE PATTERN: check:migrations compares tables, columns and CHECK constraints that admit LESS in prod, so a dropped UNIQUE adds no table, adds no column and loosens no CHECK — it reported 'in sync' with the rule still standing. Promote the code without this and prod's own database refuses the second entry with the 409 the code no longer writes, on a form that has just told the coach what their total would become. Nothing to back-fill: every existing row is already valid under the looser rule.

290_family_link_and_follower_tier_remove.note: Applied to prod 2026-09-13 ahead of the promote carrying its code (release/2026-09-13) and verified by querying production directly: 0 family_link_% columns on rep_teams, requested_player_name gone, 0 follower rows, 12 guardian links intact, both CHECKs read exactly as written (role = 'guardian'; role = 'guardian' AND player_id IS NOT NULL). ⚠ LESSON RECORDED: the deployed prod code (lib/family-access.ts on the 09-10 release) still SELECTED the dropped columns, so applying this ahead of the promote opened the family portal to column-does-not-exist errors until the new build served — prod logs showed 0 such errors in the window (quiet Sunday evening), but 'apply BEFORE the promote' for a DROP COLUMN is a live-traffic risk that this note's original text did not name; a drop-shaped order-critical migration should be applied WITH the promote (minutes before the push), not hours. Original note: The team family link and the follower tier are removed (owner, 2026-09-12). Three schema-invisible pieces: (1) a DATA-ONLY `DELETE FROM family_links WHERE role = 'follower'` — verified ZERO such rows on BOTH databases before writing the file (dev 13 links, prod 12, every one a verified guardian with a player; no team on either database had ever minted a link); (2) DROP COLUMN ×4 (rep_teams.family_link_token_hash / family_link_created_at / family_link_created_by, family_links.requested_player_name) — prod having MORE columns than dev never fails the "prod is missing" drift check; (3) two CHECKs rewritten (family_links_role_check → guardian only; family_links_role_player_ck → mig 215's strict `player_id IS NOT NULL`). ⚠ ORDER-CRITICAL: the schema-parity gate on the master build DOES see the dropped columns and the CHECK text, so the master build is red until this is on prod — apply BEFORE or WITH the promote, never after (the mig-286 lesson). Applied to dev 2026-09-12 and verified by query: both CHECKs read as written, zero family_link_% columns on rep_teams, requested_player_name gone, 13 guardian links intact. Verify on prod the same way, never by trusting this note.

291_depth_chart_three_states.sql.note: Applied to prod 2026-09-13 (with the release/2026-09-13 batch; the owner ran the apply) and verified by querying production directly with the real profile keys (the Best list is `morePreferred`, NOT `best` — a first verification query against a guessed key read every list as empty and was wrong): rows carrying canPlay 0, with_okay 0, with_best3plus 14 of 26 profiles, 0 rows with a duplicated Best position. Pre-apply Best-3+ count was not captured (the owner applied between two sessions), so 'rose by exactly the folded rows' is not provable here; what is proven is that no Okay survives, no key survives, and no fold produced a duplicate. Original note: The depth chart has three states — Best (ranked), Never, blank = fine (owner rulings D1 + D2, 2026-09-12). DATA-ONLY: each player's "Okay" (lineup_profile.canPlay) positions are appended to their Best list after the Bests they already had, in the coach's order — dropping any position already in the Best list, since the fold does not assume the app's own write-time dedup covers every row — and the canPlay key is removed from every profile. A stored JSON null in either field is treated as absent rather than crashing the migration. COUNTED BOTH DATABASES BEFORE WRITING (read-only via scripts/db-query.mjs): dev 2 players on 2 teams, prod 4 players on ONE team (9 cells) — prod's count moved to 8 players later the same day while the one team was actively editing its board, so the fold is data-driven and covers whatever is there at apply time, not this note's numbers. Applied to dev 2026-09-12 and verified by query: rows_with_key 0, with_okay 0, with_best3plus rose 0 → 2 (the two folded rows, each now Best 3 = its old Okay, no overlap on either row), with_profile unchanged at 11. /review (2026-09-12) hardened the fold's overlap-handling and null-safety after dev's apply — dev's two actual rows had zero overlap either way, so dev needs no re-run; verified the hardened logic with a synthetic 7-case test (see plan's /simplify + /review section) before this note was written. The app ignores a stray canPlay key on read and drops it on the next write, so either deploy order is safe — apply AFTER the code is on prod, then verify the same way: with_okay must read 0 and with_best3plus must have risen by exactly the folded rows (count the actual prod rows at apply time; do not assume this note's numbers). Record the numbers, never "applied".

292_development_writes_follow_the_grant..note: Applied to prod 2026-09-13 (release/2026-09-13 batch) and verified by querying production directly: 14 non-SELECT policies on the five tables, 14 named 'development writers can …', 0 named 'head coaches can …'. Original note: Development writes follow the Development GRANT (owner ruling 2026-09-11; built 2026-09-12). POLICY-ONLY: rewrites the 14 write RLS policies on rep_team_measurable_types, rep_player_measurables, rep_player_development_goals, rep_team_evaluation_sessions and rep_player_continuity_links from `coach_role = 'head_coach'` to `coach_role = 'head_coach' OR (capabilities->>'development') = 'true'` (reading rep_team_coaches.capabilities); every policy is renamed "development writers can …". SELECT policies untouched. Invisible to BOTH drift gates (a policy is not a table, column, CHECK, constraint or index) — the authoring gate learned to flag `create/drop/alter policy` in the same commit, and this was its first catch. Applied to dev 2026-09-12 and verified by query: pg_policies shows 14 non-SELECT rows on the five tables, all named "development writers can …", none "head coaches can …". RLS is not the coach portal's enforcement layer (every route runs service-role and gates on canWriteDevelopment), so prod does not 500 either way; what lags is a policy that LIES about who may write. Order-independent with the code. Verify on prod with the query at the foot of the migration file: 14 rows, none beginning "head coaches can".

295_record_and_review_both_kinds_of_deve.note: Applied to prod 2026-09-13 (release/2026-09-13 batch, after 293/294) and verified by querying production directly: the three new tables present, 12 policies across them, rep_development_goal_reviews carrying INSERT + SELECT + SELECT and nothing else, attempt_no <> 1 count 0, rep_player_measurables_session_entry_uniq gone and …_session_attempt_uniq present. Original note: Record and review both kinds of development (development lifecycle Phase 2; owner rulings 2026-09-11; /dba Finding #41; built 2026-09-13). POLICY part (invisible to both drift gates): TWELVE RLS policies on the three NEW tables — rep_evaluation_not_assessed (2 SELECT + INSERT + DELETE), rep_player_observations (2 SELECT + INSERT + UPDATE + DELETE) and rep_development_goal_reviews (2 SELECT + INSERT and NOTHING else — append-only is a policy fact: no UPDATE, no DELETE policy exists on purpose). Reads copy mig 189's two SELECT policies; writes copy mig 292's predicate (`coach_role = 'head_coach' OR (capabilities->>'development') = 'true'` on rep_team_coaches). Everything ELSE in the file is schema-VISIBLE and the parity gate sees it: attempt_no + corrected_from/_at/_by on rep_player_measurables (the partial unique `rep_player_measurables_session_entry_uniq` is DROPPED and `…_session_attempt_uniq` (session, player, type, attempt_no) created), scope_metric_ids/scope_player_ids on rep_team_evaluation_sessions, success/review_on/origin on rep_player_development_goals, the three tables with their composite (x_id, team_id) FKs, and three new uniques (rep_team_measurable_types (id, team_id) and (id, team_id, kind); rep_player_development_goals (id, team_id)) — so this file is ORDER-CRITICAL on release like 293/294 and must be applied AFTER them (the composite FK needs `kind`). No data step: every existing reading defaults to attempt 1 (the truth), every existing goal's origin is NULL (not recorded, not claimed), every existing session's scope is NULL. Applied to dev 2026-09-13 (after a first attempt rolled back on FK ordering, fixed in the file) and verified by query: pg_policies shows 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 rows on the three tables exactly as listed; `attempt_no <> 1` count 0; old index gone, new index present. Verify on prod with the query at the foot of the migration file — 12 rows, reviews carrying INSERT and nothing else — and `select count(*) from rep_player_measurables where attempt_no <> 1` → 0 right after apply.
